findings.highlight: "Let's go to Shinto. If any of the Masters is up to no good, then it'll be easier to deal with them there."
findings.evidenceJa: 「新都に行こう。物騒な事を企んでいるマスターがいるとしたら、深山より新都の方がやりやすいだろうからな」
findings.governingReading: Shirou chooses Shinto because a Master planning something dangerous would find it easier to act there than in Miyama.
findings.explanation: Shinto being easier for a hostile Master to operate in becomes easier for Shirou to deal with them there.

findings.highlight: "No, Master, your actions were correct. If a mistake was made, it was that we failed to account for your skill level.
findings.evidenceJa: 「いえ、マスターの行動自体は正しい。失点があるとしたら、シロウの技量が考えに付いてこなかっただけでしょう。
findings.governingReading: Saber says Shirou's action itself was right; if there was a shortcoming, only his ability failed to keep pace with his idea.
findings.explanation: Shirou's skill failing to match his plan becomes a shared failure to account for his skill.
